news.title: Fingerprint launches Bot Directory of AI tools, bots and crawlers
news.summary: Fingerprint launched a public directory of AI tools, bots and crawlers on September 18, 2026.

spec.title: Fingerprint launches a Bot Directory for the AI era

claims.text: On September 18, 2026, Fingerprint announced the launch of Bot Directory.
Bot Directory is a continuously updated, searchable repository of AI tools, bots, and crawlers.
evidence_terms: continuously updated, searchable repository of AI tools, bots, and crawlers

claims.text: The directory is powered by Fingerprint's Bot Detection Smart Signal and is a public resource.
The directory is public and lets you look up a bot's identity, provider, and purpose.
evidence_terms: A continuously updated directory of bots Fingerprint can detect

claims.text: Users can test their own AI agents for Web Bot Auth compliance and submit them for inclusion in the directory.
Fingerprint states that bots account for the majority of web traffic.
evidence_terms: Bots account for the majority of web traffic

claims.text: Fingerprint states that many organizations still rely on legacy bot directories built before the rise of generative AI.

scenes: Nina de la Nova, a fictional AI presenter with a soft silver bob and a dark green blazer, sits centered at a walnut podcast desk in a warm, dimly lit studio, speaking directly into a shotgun microphone. Shallow depth of field, gentle key light from the left, acoustic foam panels blurred behind her. Fully synthetic character, not resembling any real person.

Medium shot of Nina de la Nova turning slightly toward a floating holographic panel beside her desk, listing rows of bot names, providers, and purposes in cool blue text. She gestures calmly at the list while the studio stays warm and softly lit. Fully synthetic character, not resembling any real person.

Over-the-shoulder shot of Nina de la Nova at her studio desk, a large screen ahead showing a search and filter interface with a verified badge glowing next to one entry. Slow push in, ambient amber and teal lighting, steady and unhurried mood. Fully synthetic character, not resembling any real person.

Close-up of Nina de la Nova facing the camera, hands resting on the desk, delivering the closing line with a small reassuring nod. Studio lights dim slightly, a faint on-screen caption bar reads AI generated presenter. Fully synthetic character, not resembling any real person.
spec.script: Here is something worth knowing if you run a website. On September 18, 2026, Fingerprint announced the launch of Bot Directory, a continuously updated, searchable repository of AI tools, bots, and crawlers. It is powered by Fingerprint's Bot Detection Smart Signal, and the directory is public, so you can look up a bot's identity, provider, and purpose yourself. You can also test your own AI agent for Web Bot Auth compliance and submit it for inclusion. Fingerprint points out that bots account for the majority of web traffic, and that many organizations still lean on legacy bot directories built before the rise of generative AI. If automated traffic is reaching your site, this gives you a calm place to start looking.
